name: MonarchAiMessageBranch
title: AiMessageBranch
wrapsNative: Button with MonarchButtonStyle (ghost, sm) and Text in an HStack
summary: The previous, position, next switcher between alternative versions of a message, made when a reply is regenerated or a prompt is edited and resent.
whenToUse: Under a message that has more than one version, bound to the version that is shown.
whenNotToUse: Not for paging through a list: use the system page controls. Not for a number a person sets: use the standard Stepper.
api: init(selection: Binding<Int>, count: Int, showsSingle: Bool = false, label: String? = nil, previousLabel: String? = nil, nextLabel: String? = nil, formatPosition: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, formatAnnouncement: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: showsSingle
options.description: Shows the switcher when there is only one version.

options.name: previousLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Previous version".

options.name: nextLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Next version".

options.name: formatPosition
options.description: Replaces the built-in visible position "2 / 3". Receives the version, counted from 1, and the count.

options.name: formatAnnouncement
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken position "Version 2 of 3".

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true) both buttons are disabled and the position uses the disabled text role.

states.name: hidden
states.description: With fewer than two versions nothing is shown, unless showsSingle is true.

appearance: Two ghost buttons with chevrons and a muted caption between them, in tabular digits so the buttons do not move. Colours are the ghost button roles and the muted text role of the theme.
platformNotes: The web is controlled with index and onChange; here it is a Binding, the SwiftUI convention. The web's disabled prop is the standard disabled(_:) modifier. The web moves keyboard focus to the other button when one becomes disabled at an end; this is not done here, because VoiceOver keeps its focus on a button that becomes dimmed.
accessibility: A group named "Versions" that contains the two buttons and the position.
The buttons are named "Previous version" and "Next version"; each has a 44-point touch target.
The position is read as "Version 2 of 3", not as "2 / 3".
After a button changes the version, the new position is announced. A change made elsewhere is not announced.
The chevrons are the backward and forward symbols, so they mirror in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A selection outside the range is shown as the nearest version; a step then starts from the version shown.
A count below 1 is treated as 1.
Large counts widen the position; the buttons keep their size.

examples.title: Switch between versions
examples.template:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: theme.spacing.space2) {
    Text(versions[version])
        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
        .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textDefault)
    MonarchAiMessageBranch(selection: $version, count: versions.count)
}
.padding(.horizontal)
